nodes.What it is: Before a robot works near people, engineers list what could hurt someone (hazards), estimate how bad and how likely it is, and add measures until the remaining risk is acceptable. International standards give the vocabulary and method: ISO 12100 for machines in general, ISO 10218 for industrial robots, ISO 13482 for personal-care robots.
nodes.Prerequisites: None for reading; basic notion of how a robot arm moves helps.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: ISO 10218-1:2025 (Edition 3) and ISO 10218-2:2025 (Edition 2) were published in 2025-02. ISO/TS 15066:2016 (collaborative robots) was confirmed in 2022 and remains current, but ISO lists it as "to be revised" and to be replaced by ISO/AWI 15066-1 (under development). ISO 12100:2010 is expected to be replaced by ISO/DIS 12100.3, and ISO 13482:2014 is also marked as expected to be replaced. Full texts are paid; only catalogue abstracts were read.
nodes.Key players: ISO (standards publisher); robot makers that document certified safety functions, e.g. Universal Robots
nodes.Best resources: ISO catalogue pages for ISO 12100, 10218-1/-2, 13482 ; Bartneck et al., Human-Robot Interaction: An Introduction (free site)

nodes.What it is: A collaborative robot (cobot) shares space with people. Standards describe ways to make this safe, including power and force limiting (contact is allowed but forces stay below limits) and speed and separation monitoring (the robot slows or stops as a person gets closer). Which mode fits comes from the risk assessment, not from the robot label.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: ISO/TS 15066:2016 supplements ISO 10218-1/-2 for collaborative industrial robot systems and does not apply to non-industrial robots. Research cited in 2024-2026 papers uses ISO 10218-2:2025 contact thresholds; one 2026 paper reports that the blunt-impact data does not cover edged or pointed collisions.
nodes.Key players: Universal Robots (configurable safety limits, always-active power and force limiting); Franka Robotics; CTU Prague and TU Munich research groups (from opened papers)
nodes.Best resources: ISO/TS 15066 abstract ; arXiv 1908.03046 (unified SSM + PFL) ; arXiv 1805.07256

nodes.What it is: Human-robot interaction (HRI) studies how people and robots communicate and work together. Because "it felt natural" is not evidence, HRI uses user studies: questionnaires, behaviour measurements and sometimes physiological signals, with a clear protocol and statistics. Perceived safety (whether people feel safe) is measured separately from physical safety.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: The ACM/IEEE HRI conference ran its 21st edition (HRI 2026, Edinburgh, March 16-19, 2026) and announces Santa Clara for the next one. A survey lists questionnaires, physiological measurements, behavioural assessment and direct input devices to assess perceived safety.
nodes.Key players: ACM/IEEE HRI conference community; Bartneck et al. (textbook authors); Furhat Robotics (research platform)
nodes.Best resources: Human-Robot Interaction: An Introduction (book site) ; free edX/UCx HRI Professional Certificate ; arXiv 2105.14499 (perceived safety survey)

nodes.Node: Human detection & body-pose tracking for HRI
nodes.What it is: To react to people, a robot must first see them: where they are and how their body is posed. Pose estimators output keypoints (joints like wrists and shoulders) from a camera image, which later layers turn into distances, gestures or safety zones.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Off-the-shelf models run in real time: MediaPipe Pose Landmarker tracks 33 3D body landmarks and runs in the browser via WebAssembly; Ultralytics documents YOLO26 pose models pretrained on COCO keypoints. Research uses RGB-D cameras, lidar or on-robot ranging sensors for separation distance. None of these camera models is safety-rated.
nodes.Key players: Google (MediaPipe); Ultralytics; robotics labs using RGB-D/lidar for HRC distance
nodes.Best resources: MediaPipe Pose Landmarker docs ; Ultralytics pose docs ; arXiv 1810.04953 (RGB-D separation distance)

nodes.What it is: Speed and separation monitoring means continuously measuring the distance between robot and human and lowering the robot speed (or stopping) so it can always stop before contact. Building it needs sensors, a distance computation between robot links and the person, and a speed-scaling rule.
nodes.Prerequisites: Collaborative operation modes (cobots); Human detection & body-pose tracking for HRI
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Research prototypes use time-of-flight sensor arrays on robot links, RGB-D cameras and 3D lidar; a 2025 study compares neural networks for learning safety speed reduction and a 2026 paper sizes protective zones from operator presence data. These are research results, not certified safety functions.
nodes.Key players: Research labs publishing on SSM (from opened arXiv papers); industrial safety-sensor vendors (not researched)

nodes.Node: Collision detection & reaction (power and force limiting)
nodes.What it is: If contact cannot be avoided, the robot must notice a collision (for example from joint torques or a sensitive skin) and react, such as stopping or becoming compliant. Power and force limiting keeps contact forces and pressures below thresholds that depend on the body region.
nodes.Prerequisites: Collaborative operation modes (cobots); basic robot dynamics
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Recent work makes thresholds adaptive: per-link effective mass with a UR10e and AIRSKIN skin (2024), reachability-based shields with formal guarantees (SARA shield, 2024), and injury databases extended to shearing contacts (2026). Low-cost smart servos are not designed or certified for this.
nodes.Key players: Universal Robots; Franka Robotics; CTU Prague (Hoffmann group, adaptive sensitivity); TU Munich (SARA shield)

nodes.What it is: In shared control, a human gives commands (joystick, teleoperation) and the robot blends them with its own autonomy, for example to help a person with motor impairments grasp a cup. The robot must infer what the human wants and decide how much to assist.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Deep RL can learn shared autonomy without assuming known goals (2018). 2026 papers explore legible shared autonomy (robot motion reveals its belief), capability-aware arbitration and blended shared control inside interactive imitation learning.
nodes.Key players: UC Berkeley (Reddy, Dragan, Levine); HRI and RSS communities

nodes.What it is: Kinesthetic teaching means a person physically moves the robot by hand to show a task, and the robot records the motion. It needs the robot to be compliant (it yields when pushed) and to compensate its own weight so it is easy and safe to guide.
nodes.Prerequisites: Collaborative operation modes (cobots); joint torque or current sensing basics
nodes.Frontier state 2026: 2024-2026 papers add mixed-reality feedback, observer-based hand-guiding with active support, force guidance and tactile data (KineDex) to kinesthetic teaching, and use it as a demonstration source for imitation and RL.
nodes.Key players: Franka Robotics (FCI research interface); research labs (from opened papers)
nodes.Best resources: Franka Control Interface docs ; arXiv 2409.02305 ; arXiv 2608.10847

nodes.What it is: A handover is passing an object between a robot and a person. It has a pre-handover phase (agreeing where and when, often implicitly) and a physical exchange that ends when the giver fully releases the object.
nodes.Prerequisites: Human detection & body-pose tracking for HRI; basic grasping
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Simulation benchmarks exist for human-to-robot (HandoverSim, 2022) and robot-to-human handovers (R2HandoverSim, 2026); 2025 work learns dexterous handovers.
nodes.Key players: Monash/QUT authors of the handover review; NVIDIA-affiliated HandoverSim authors (not verified as organizations)

nodes.What it is: Legible motion makes the robot intent obvious early, for example reaching in an exaggerated arc so a person guesses the target sooner. Predictable motion is what people expect; Dragan et al. showed the two are different and can conflict.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Legibility is extended to cluttered scenes, service-robot local planners (Legibot), comparisons with body-language cues (2026) and hallway navigation studies.
nodes.Best resources: Dragan et al., Legibility and Predictability of Robot Motion (HRI 2013) ; arXiv 2404.05100 ; arXiv 2604.03451

nodes.What it is: A mobile robot among people must reach its goal while respecting personal space, not cutting through groups and staying predictable. Evaluating this is hard because it depends on how humans perceive the robot.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: A 2023 multi-author paper proposes principles and guidelines for evaluating social navigation. ROS 2 tools such as HuNavSim (2.0 in 2025, wrappers for Gazebo, Isaac Sim and Webots) and Arena 4.0/5.0 provide human simulation and benchmarking; 2024-2026 work adds LLM-based scenario generation and reasoning.
nodes.Key players: Universidad Pablo de Olavide (HuNavSim); Arena-Rosnav team; Google and academic co-authors of the guidelines
nodes.Sources:
https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.16740
https://github.com/robotics-upo/hunav_sim
https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.01303
https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.12471
https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11220
https://docs.nav2.org/rolling/

nodes.What it is: Robots can now talk: speech recognition turns voice into text, a language model decides what to say or do, and the robot answers with voice, gestures and head motion. Timing (turn-taking, interruptions) and matching gestures to speech are what make it feel natural.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Open speech recognition (Whisper, MIT license) and LLMs make prototypes quick. 2026 papers address full-duplex interaction with interruptible motion (MIRA) and co-speech gesture generation for humanoids. Reachy Mini (Pollen Robotics and Hugging Face) is sold as an open-source HRI robot, Lite version listed at $399 plus taxes and shipping.
nodes.Key players: Pollen Robotics and Hugging Face (Reachy Mini, Paris); Furhat Robotics; Google DeepMind (Gemini Robotics)
nodes.Best resources: Reachy Mini blog and SDK ; Whisper repo ; arXiv 2404.00938 (LLMs for socially assistive HRI)

nodes.What it is: To move safely and helpfully, robots predict where people will walk or reach next, a few seconds ahead. Methods range from simple physics-like models (social forces) to deep networks trained on trajectory datasets.
nodes.Prerequisites: Human detection & body-pose tracking for HRI; basic ML
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Trajectron++ (ECCV 2020, MIT license) is a reference open model; 2023 work revisits the Social Force Model for low-compute prediction; 2026 papers target prediction specifically for human-robot collaboration.

nodes.Node: Robotics regulation & compliance in the EU
nodes.What it is: Selling or deploying a robot in Europe means following laws, not just standards. The new Machinery Regulation replaces the old Machinery Directive, and the AI Act adds rules for AI systems, including AI used as a safety component of products such as machinery.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 applies from 14 January 2027 (some articles earlier). The AI Act (EU) 2024/1689 lists machinery among product legislation where AI systems can be high-risk. This is a legal summary from the official texts, not legal advice.
nodes.Key players: European Commission; notified bodies; national market-surveillance authorities
nodes.Best resources: EUR-Lex text of Regulation 2023/1230 ; EUR-Lex text of Regulation 2024/1689

nodes.What it is: Learned policies can do unexpected things. A safety filter sits between the policy and the motors and minimally changes unsafe commands; control barrier functions (CBFs) are a common mathematical tool. Safe RL adds constraints during learning.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: A 2021 review unifies learning-based control and safe RL; safe-control-gym provides PyBullet benchmarks with symbolic constraints and disturbances (MIT license). 2026 papers add multi-link safety filtering for VLA policies around moving hazards and safety-constrained MPC.
nodes.Key players: University of Toronto / TUM Learning Systems lab (safe-control-gym); Caltech and others (CBF theory)

nodes.Node: Semantic safety & guardrails for LLM/VLA-controlled robots
nodes.What it is: When a language or vision-language model controls a robot, safety is also about meaning: refusing a harmful instruction, or noticing that a hot pan should not be handed to a child. Guardrails check plans against safety rules, and benchmarks test whether models judge situations safely.
nodes.Prerequisites: LLM prompting and APIs; basic robot task planning
nodes.Frontier state 2026: RoboPAIR (ICRA 2025) jailbroke LLM-controlled robots including a Unitree Go2, often with 100% attack success. RoboGuard (2025) proposes a two-stage guardrail. Google DeepMind released the ASIMOV benchmark (CoRL 2025) for semantic safety of robot foundation models. 2026 papers propose modular guardrails and diagnostic VLA safety benchmarks.
nodes.Key players: University of Pennsylvania (RoboPAIR, RoboGuard); Google DeepMind (ASIMOV, Gemini Robotics)
nodes.Best resources: ASIMOV benchmark page ; RoboPAIR page ; arXiv 2503.07885 (RoboGuard)
nodes.Sources:
https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.13691
https://robopair.org/
https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.07885
https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.08663
https://asimov-benchmark.github.io/v1/
https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.04056
https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27079

nodes.What it is: Instead of only learning from demonstrations collected beforehand, the robot learns while acting: a human corrects it, takes over, or ranks behaviours. Interactive imitation learning and RL from human feedback reduce the gap between what was shown and what the robot actually does.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: A 2022 survey structures interactive imitation learning; a 2025 survey covers it for dexterous humanoid manipulation; 2026 work includes blended shared control for interactive IL and a scoping review of RLHF for human-robot collaboration.
nodes.Key players: TU Delft and co-authors (IIL survey); robot-learning labs

nodes.Node: Safety of humanoids & dynamically stable mobile robots
nodes.What it is: A walking robot cannot simply be switched off when something goes wrong: cutting power makes it fall, which is itself a hazard. Safety for humanoids and self-balancing robots therefore needs new standards and controlled stopping behaviours.
nodes.Prerequisites: Robot safety standards & risk assessment; locomotion basics
nodes.Frontier state 2026: ISO/CD 25785-1 (safety requirements for dynamically stable industrial mobile robots, legged or wheeled) is under development. A 2026 paper names the fail-passive gap and pinpoints the robot-side reaction chain as the part not yet certifiable. Unitree G1 is listed from US $13.5K.
nodes.Key players: ISO TC 299 working groups (not verified in detail); humanoid makers such as Unitree
nodes.Best resources: ISO search result for 25785 ; arXiv 2608.02809 ; arXiv 2511.23300

Knowledge nodes: Collision detection & reaction (power and force limiting)

robots_models.Name: ASIMOV Benchmark
Knowledge nodes: Semantic safety & guardrails for LLM/VLA-controlled robots

robots_models.Key specs: Benchmarks and generated robot constitutions for semantic safety of robot foundation models; accepted at CoRL 2025
robots_models.Why it matters: Public benchmark to test whether an LLM/VLA judges physical situations safely.

robots_models.Name: RoboPAIR
Knowledge nodes: Semantic safety & guardrails for LLM/VLA-controlled robots
robots_models.Price / access: Paper and project page; code availability not verified
robots_models.Key specs: Jailbreak algorithm for LLM-controlled robots tested on simulators, a Clearpath Jackal UGV and Unitree Go2

robots_models.Name: RoboGuard
Knowledge nodes: Semantic safety & guardrails for LLM/VLA-controlled robots
robots_models.Key specs: Two-stage guardrail: root-of-trust LLM contextualizes rules, then temporal-logic control synthesis checks plans
